target.title: fix(agents): suppress unhandled rejection from async abort callback
target.body:
## Summary

Add `.catch()` with a `process.stderr.write` diagnostic to the agent session extension abort callback. If `session.abort()` ever rejects, the rejection is logged instead of surfacing as an unhandled rejection.

This is a **defense-in-depth** hardening change. `Agent.waitForIdle()` currently resolves the active run promise, so the rejecting path is not reproducible under normal runtime conditions. The catch guards the fire-and-forget extension callback boundary so that a future regression or an extension-provided `extensionAbortHandler` override that delegates here cannot crash the process.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

**Behavior addressed**: `void this.abort()` in the extension callback could leave a rejected promise unhandled if `session.abort()` ever rejects.

**Real environment tested**: Linux, Node 22, OpenClaw branch `fix/agent-session-void-abort-catch`

**Proof command**:
```bash
node_modules/.bin/tsx scripts/proof/agent-session-abort-catch.mts
```

**Proof script output** (scripts/proof/agent-session-abort-catch.mts):
```
=== Proof: agent session extension abort catch ===

Calling extension runtime abort callback with a rejecting session.abort()...

agent-session: extension abort failed: Error: simulated abort rejection

PASS: rejecting abort is caught and logged instead of becoming an unhandled rejection.
```

The proof creates a real `AgentSession`, stubs its `abort()` to reject, invokes the bound extension runtime `abortFn`, and captures stderr to show the diagnostic is written.

**Regression test**:
```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/sessions/agent-session.test.ts
```

```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed (1)
```

The regression test "logs a diagnostic when the extension abort fallback rejects" exercises the same synthetic rejecting-abort path and asserts the stderr diagnostic.

**Why stderr instead of the extension error-reporting path**: the abort callback is fire-and-forget (`void ...`) and runs when the extension runtime may already be tearing down. `process.stderr.write` is the lowest-level, synchronous sink available and matches other emergency diagnostics in the session boundary. The extension error listener is not used because the callback must not itself throw or await async reporting.

## Risk

Low. Error logged to stderr for observability; no change to happy-path behavior.
